description: SIE Enterprise Ontology & Data Model Expansion v0.1 -- the durable, version-controlled, PII-free record of the ontology-gap investigation performed against the 15 real-dataset terminology terms that remain REJECTED in backend/config/real_enterprise_terminology_decisions_v1.json. Each entry here documents ONE ontology gap investigation and its outcome: either a new, platform-wide OntologyConcept (APPROVED) that a FUTURE, separately governed terminology-mapping decision could someday target, or a deliberate decision that no new concept is justified (REJECTED -- the gap remains a genuine, documented limitation, not silently resolved). Applying this artifact NEVER creates, modifies, or reprocesses a TerminologyMappingDecision or a SafetyEvent -- see app/services/ontology_concept_artifact_service.py's own docstring. No real record IDs, names, narratives, emails, or phone numbers; no real database UUIDs (concept IDs are generated fresh by OntologyConcept every time this artifact is applied).

concepts.definition: An Incident-domain event whose primary characteristic is an uncontrolled fire or combustion event (ignition, spread, or fire-suppression-system activation), distinct from an ENVIRONMENTAL_EVENT (a spill or environmental release) or any other existing INCIDENT subtype.
concepts.existing_equivalent: None. The existing INCIDENT subtype vocabulary (FIRST_AID_CASE, MEDICAL_TREATMENT_CASE, LOST_TIME_INCIDENT, VEHICLE_INCIDENT, PROPERTY_DAMAGE, ENVIRONMENTAL_EVENT) has no fire-specific value; ENVIRONMENTAL_EVENT's own aliases ('environmental event', 'spill') are semantically about environmental releases, not fire.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 4 occurrences of the raw Incident Type term 'FireIncident'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Fire is a universal, high-severity, clearly distinct HSE incident category with no existing canonical equivalent; representing it accurately has clear future intelligence value (fire-specific leading/lagging indicators) and is fully generalizable across any enterprise customer, not specific to this one.
concepts.impact: Additive only. No existing SafetyEvent, TerminologyMappingDecision, or intelligence feature is affected -- this concept is not wired into any terminology mapping or ingestion path by this milestone. A future, separately governed terminology-mapping decision could target FIRE for the rejected 'FireIncident' term; not done here.

concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 3 occurrences of the raw Incident Type term 'Others'.
concepts.why_no_new_concept: A catch-all term is, by construction, never semantically exact -- it explicitly denotes 'not clearly any of the other categories'. No single canonical concept can represent an undefined residual category without guessing at its actual meaning per-record, which this milestone's naming rules (one defined semantic meaning) forbid.
concepts.impact: None -- this gap remains permanently undecidable at the ontology level; resolving individual 'Others' records, if ever done, would require per-record human review, not a new canonical concept.

concepts.evidence: Real dataset: only 2 occurrences of the raw Incident Type term 'SecurityBreach'; no narrative content was ever loaded or reviewed (PII policy), so the actual meaning (physical site-security incident vs. a data/cyber security event, which would be entirely outside SIE's HSE scope) cannot be determined from the terminology alone.
concepts.why_no_new_concept: Genuinely ambiguous scope (is 'security' here a physical-safety/HSSE concern, which could belong in this ontology, or a cyber/data-security concern, which is out of scope for a Safety Intelligence Engine?) combined with thin evidence (2 occurrences) does not meet this milestone's own bar ('only add concepts justified by... real enterprise evidence... clear semantic distinction'). Introducing a canonical value on this little evidence risks defining the wrong concept.
concepts.impact: None. Documented as an open ontology gap requiring more evidence (or direct clarification from a real HSE reviewer) before a future milestone could responsibly propose a concept here.

concepts.existing_equivalent: The existing top-level OBSERVATION event_type already represents exactly this concept.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: only 1 occurrence of the raw Incident Type term 'HazardObservation'.
concepts.why_no_new_concept: This reads as a data-entry/categorization mismatch (a hazard observation logged on the Incident sheet) rather than a genuine ontology gap -- SIE's ontology already has a dedicated, well-populated OBSERVATION event_type for exactly this concept. Inventing an INCIDENT-domain concept to match the sheet it happened to be entered on would encode a source-system data-quality quirk into the canonical ontology, which this milestone's naming rules explicitly forbid ('not depend on a particular customer's terminology').
concepts.impact: None. If ever revisited, the correct fix is very likely a data-quality/source-mapping correction at the terminology layer (routing this term toward the existing OBSERVATION event_type), never a new INCIDENT-domain concept -- a determination for a future milestone, not made here.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning work performed at height (falls, fall-protection equipment, edge protection, etc.) -- a subject-matter tag on an OBSERVATION, never itself a finding/condition type (contrast the existing event_subtype value UNSAFE_CONDITION, which is the *kind of finding*, orthogonal to this *topic*).
concepts.existing_equivalent: PERMIT's own WORK_AT_HEIGHT subtype exists, but it classifies a permit-to-work record, a structurally different concept (an authorization document) from an Observation's own topic tag. Reusing it here would be exactly the cross-domain substitution this milestone forbids.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 128 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Working At Height' -- the single largest unresolved term in the entire real dataset.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Very high real-world evidence and volume; a universal, high-value HSE activity category; genuinely distinct from the existing PERMIT-domain subtype and from every existing OBSERVATION finding-type value.
concepts.impact: Additive only. Introduces a NEW ontology layer, observation_topic, orthogonal to event_subtype -- documented in docs/SIE_ENTERPRISE_ONTOLOGY_V0_1.md's own 'Observation semantic model' section. No existing SafetyEvent, mapping, or intelligence feature reads this layer yet; wiring it into terminology mapping/ingestion is explicitly deferred to a future milestone.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning personal protective equipment generally (both compliant and non-compliant instances) -- a subject-matter tag, distinct from the existing event_subtype value PPE_ISSUE (a specific negative finding).
concepts.existing_equivalent: PPE_ISSUE exists as an OBSERVATION event_subtype but denotes a specific negative finding only ('ppe issue'/'ppe non compliance' aliases) -- not an exact equivalent for the broader topic/category this term represents (already investigated in depth in the Terminology Calibration v0.1 corrective commit's own PPE Compliance ontology-limitation finding).
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 117 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'PPE Compliance' -- the second-largest unresolved term in the entire real dataset.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: This is precisely the semantic-layer distinction this milestone exists to make: 'topic/category' (what the observation is about) is a genuinely different dimension from 'finding/condition' (what was found) -- see docs/SIE_ENTERPRISE_ONTOLOGY_V0_1.md's own boundary rules. Very high evidence volume and clear, generalizable, non-customer-specific value.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above. Directly closes the ontology gap the corrective commit documented for 'PPE Compliance' -- but the rejected TerminologyMappingDecision for 'PPE Compliance' is NOT changed by this artifact; remapping it against this new concept is explicitly the next milestone's decision.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning electrical hazards or electrical-work safety practices.
concepts.existing_equivalent: None. No existing SIE canonical value (event_type, event_subtype, or otherwise) represents electrical-safety-as-a-topic.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 47 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Electrical Safety'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Universal, high-value, clearly distinct HSE topic with substantial real evidence and no existing canonical overlap.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning environmental hazards or environmental-management practices -- a topic tag on an OBSERVATION record specifically, in the observation_topic layer's own namespace (deliberately distinct from, and never confused with, the existing top-level ENVIRONMENTAL SafetyEventType or the existing INCIDENT subtype ENVIRONMENTAL_EVENT, both of which classify an EVENT, not an observation's topic).
concepts.existing_equivalent: The top-level ENVIRONMENTAL event_type and the INCIDENT subtype ENVIRONMENTAL_EVENT both exist, but classify a different kind of thing (an event that happened), not an Observation's own topic/category -- not an exact equivalent for this layer.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 32 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Environmental'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Same topic-vs-event semantic-layer distinction as PPE_COMPLIANCE above; the name collision with existing values in OTHER layers is deliberate and namespaced (layer+parent_domain+concept_key is the real scope key, not concept_key alone) -- documented explicitly in docs/SIE_ENTERPRISE_ONTOLOGY_V0_1.md to avoid any future confusion.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning crane, hoist, or other lifting-equipment operations.
concepts.existing_equivalent: PERMIT's own LIFTING_OPERATION subtype exists, but classifies a permit-to-work record, a structurally different concept from an Observation's own topic tag -- reusing it here would be the same cross-domain substitution WORKING_AT_HEIGHT's own entry describes.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 31 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Lifting Operations'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Universal, high-value HSE activity category with substantial real evidence, genuinely distinct from the existing PERMIT-domain subtype.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.

concepts.definition: An Observation-domain finding/condition type: a documented instance of non-compliance with a defined operating procedure or work instruction -- a finding-type concept (like the existing UNSAFE_ACT/UNSAFE_CONDITION), never a topic/category.
concepts.existing_equivalent: None. The existing OBSERVATION event_subtype vocabulary (UNSAFE_ACT, UNSAFE_CONDITION, POSITIVE_OBSERVATION, HOUSEKEEPING_DEFICIENCY, PPE_ISSUE) has no procedure-compliance-specific value.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 29 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Procedure Violation'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Unlike the other Observation-domain gaps investigated here, this term genuinely describes a FINDING (what was found), not a topic (what it was about) -- correctly belongs in the SAME existing event_subtype layer as UNSAFE_ACT/UNSAFE_CONDITION, extending that vocabulary with one clearly distinct, generalizable new finding-type rather than introducing a new layer.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above -- extends the event_subtype layer's OBSERVATION vocabulary rather than the new observation_topic layer, demonstrating the milestone's own required semantic-layer determination in practice.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning equipment-related hazards or equipment-safety practices (distinct from the existing top-level EQUIPMENT event_type, which classifies equipment maintenance/status events, not an observation's topic).
concepts.existing_equivalent: The top-level EQUIPMENT event_type exists but classifies a different kind of thing (a maintenance/status event) -- not an exact equivalent for an Observation's own topic tag.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 13 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Equipment Safety'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Same topic-vs-event distinction as ENVIRONMENTAL above; clearly distinct, generalizable HSE topic.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.

concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 13 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Others'.
concepts.why_no_new_concept: Same reasoning as the Incident-domain 'Others' entry above -- a catch-all term is never semantically exact by construction. Independently scoped from the event_type-domain 'Others' term (never collapsed into one global decision, matching the terminology artifact's own independent-scoping rule).
concepts.impact: None -- permanently undecidable at the ontology level.

concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 11 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Documentation'.
concepts.why_no_new_concept: Ambiguous and low generalizable safety-value: 'Documentation' could mean a records-completeness finding, a paperwork/administrative process topic, or something specific to this one organization's own recordkeeping practice -- unlike the other approved topics (PPE, electrical, fire, height, lifting, equipment, environmental, emergency preparedness), it does not clearly name a distinct, universal HSE hazard/activity domain. Does not meet this milestone's own 'clear semantic distinction' and 'future intelligence value' bar with the evidence available.
concepts.impact: None. Documented as an open gap; a future milestone could reconsider with clearer evidence of what this term actually represents in practice.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning fire-safety practices, fire-prevention measures, or fire-protection equipment (distinct from the FIRE event_subtype above, which classifies an actual fire INCIDENT that occurred, not an observation's topic).
concepts.existing_equivalent: None in the observation_topic layer. The new FIRE event_subtype concept (above) is a different layer classifying a different kind of thing (an incident that happened, not an observation's topic).
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 4 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Fire Safety'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: Universal, high-value HSE topic with a clear, distinct meaning from every existing value and from the new FIRE incident-subtype concept.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.

concepts.definition: The safety topic/activity category of an Observation record concerning emergency-response planning, drills, or preparedness measures.
concepts.evidence: Real dataset: 2 occurrences of the raw Observation Category term 'Emergency Preparedness'.
concepts.why_new_concept_required: A universal, well-defined, generalizable HSE topic (emergency preparedness is a standard HSE management-system element) despite relatively low occurrence count in this one dataset -- unlike SecurityBreach, the concept's meaning is unambiguous and its safety-management value is well established industry-wide, not dependent on this one customer's own usage.
concepts.impact: Additive only, same as WORKING_AT_HEIGHT above.
